name: Read
description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

name: Write
description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

content.description: The content to write to the file

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

name: Edit
description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

name: Bash
description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached.

# Git
- Interactive flags are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words). For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags), add enough context to clarify what it does.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

name: Skill
description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`.
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing are valid.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

name: ToolSearch
description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in system-reminder messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

name: Agent
description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in system-reminder messages.

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment.

mode.description: Deprecated; ignored. Subagents inherit the parent session's permission mode.

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter.

name.description: Name for the spawned agent. Makes it addressable via SendMessage.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

team_name.description: Deprecated; ignored. The session has a single implicit team.

name: Artifact
description:
Render an HTML or Markdown file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai that the user can later choose to share with their teammates. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text.

**Title**: Set a `<title>` at the top of the HTML. It names the artifact in the browser tab and gallery.

**To update**: Edit the file, then call Artifact again with the same file path — it redeploys to the same URL.

**Self-contained only**: A strict CSP blocks requests to any external host. Inline all CSS/JS and embed assets as data: URIs.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller.

**Theme-aware**: Pages render in the viewer's theme.

**Favicon** (required): Pass one or two emoji as `favicon`.

action.description: Omit (or 'publish') to publish file_path. 'list' enumerates artifacts. 'comments' reads the comment threads on a published artifact. 'reply' posts a reply into one comment thread. 'resolve' marks one comment thread resolved.

capabilities.description: Runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. The control plane is the authority on valid names and config shapes.

contract.description: The artifact's runtime version. Omit to keep its current version (the default); 'latest' to upgrade; a specific version to pin or roll back.

cursor.description: comments only: continue a listing that ended with a "more threads not listed" line.

description.description: One-sentence subtitle shown on the gallery card. Say what the page is or does.

favicon.description: Browser-tab icon: one or two emoji (e.g. "📊"). No markup. Required to publish.

file_path.description: Path to an .html or .md file to render. Required to publish (the default action).

force.description: Last-resort overwrite that DISCARDS another session's published version.

label.description: Short human-readable name for this version, max 60 chars (e.g. "fixed-background").

limit.description: list only: maximum artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list only: 'mine' (default) lists artifacts the user owns; 'shared' lists artifacts other people shared with the user; 'all' lists both.

text.description: reply only: the reply text. Plain text, at most 4096 bytes of UTF-8.

thread_id.description: reply: id of the comment thread to reply into. resolve: the thread to mark resolved.

title.description: Title for the artifact — the name shown in the browser tab and gallery.

url.description: Existing artifact URL to update in place. Omit for new artifacts and same-conversation redeploys.
